source_text: Ὑπόδειγμα δ’ ἡμῖν κατὰ παραδρομὴν ἐκκείσθω εἰς σαφήνειαν γνωστικὴν ἡ δεκάλογος. καὶ ὅτι μὲν ἱερὰ ἡ δεκάς, παρέλκει λέγειν τὰ νῦν. εἰ δὲ αἱ πλάκες αἱ γεγραμμέναι ἔργον θεοῦ, φυσικὴν ἐμφαίνουσαι δημιουργίαν εὑρεθήσονται· δάκτυλος γὰρ θεοῦ δύναμις νοεῖται θεοῦ, δἰ ἧς ἡ κτίσις τελειοῦται οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς, ὧν ἀμφοῖν αἱ πλάκες νοηθήσονται σύμβολα. θεοῦ μὲν γὰρ γραφὴ καὶ εἰδοποιία ἐναποκειμένη τῇ πλακὶ δημιουργία τοῦ κόσμου τυγχάνει. ἡ δεκάλογος δὲ κατὰ μὲν οὐράνιον εἰκόνα περιέχει ἥλιον καὶ σελήνην, ἄστρα, νέφη, φῶς, πνεῦμα, ὕδωρ, ἀέρα, σκότος, πῦρ. αὕτη φυσικὴ δεκάλογος οὐρανοῦ. ἡ δὲ τῆς γῆς εἰκὼν περιέχει ἀνθρώπους, κτήνη, ἑρπετά, θηρία καὶ τῶν ἐνύδρων ἰχθύας καὶ κήτη, τῶν τε αὖ πτηνῶν ὁμοίως τά τε σαρκοβόρα καὶ τὰ ἡμέρῳ χρώμενα τροφῇ, φυτῶν τε ὡσαύτως τὰ καρποφόρα καὶ ἄκαρπα. αὕτη φυσικὴ δεκάλογος γῆς. καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς δὲ ἡ ταῦτα περιειληφυῖα ἡ τῶν θείων τε καὶ ἀνθρωπίνων γνῶσις εἴη ἂν καὶ σοφία. τάχα δ’ ἃν εἶεν αἱ δύο πλάκες αὗται δισσῶν προφητεία διαθηκῶν. ἀνεκαινίσθησαν οὖν μυστικῶς, πλεοναζούσης ἀγνοίας ἅμα καὶ ἁμαρτίας. δισσῶς, ὡς ἔοικεν, γράφονται δισσοῖς πνεύμασιν ἐντολαί, τῷ τε ἡγεμονικῷ τῷ τε ὑποκειμένῳ, ἐπεὶ ἡ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα κατὰ τῆς σαρκός. ἔστι δὲ καὶ δεκάς τις περὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον αὐτόν, τά τε αἰσθητήρια πέντε καὶ τὸ φωνητικὸν καὶ τὸ σπερματικὸν καὶ τοῦτο δὴ ὄγδοον τὸ κατὰ τὴν πλάσιν πνευματικόν, ἔνατον δὲ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ δέκατον τὸ διὰ τῆς πίστεως προσγινόμενον ἁγίου πνεύματος χαρακτηριστικὸν ἰδίωμα. ἔτι πρὸς τούτοις δέκα τισὶν ἀνθρωπείοις μέρεσι προστάσσειν ἡ νομοθεσία φαίνεται, τῇ τε ὁράσει καὶ ἀκοῇ καὶ τῇ ὀσφρήσει ἁφῇ τε καὶ γεύσει καὶ τοῖς τούτων ὑπουργοῖς ὀργάνοις δισσοῖς οὖσι, χερσί τε καὶ ποσίν· αὕτη γὰρ ἡ πλάσις τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. ἐπεισκρίνεται δὲ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ προσεισκρίνεται τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, ᾧ διαλογιζόμεθα, οὐ κατὰ τὴν τοῦ σπέρματος καταβολὴν γεννώμενον, ὡς συνάγεσθαι καὶ ἄνευ τούτου τὸν δέκατον ἀριθμόν, δἰ ὧν ἡ πᾶσα ἐνέργεια τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπιτελεῖται. τῇ τάξει γὰρ εὐθέως γενόμενος. ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀπὸ τῶν παθητικῶν τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ ζῆν λαμβάνει. τὸ λογιστικὸν τοίνυν καὶ ἡγεμονικὸν αἴτιον εἶναί φαμεν τῆς συστάσεως τῷ ζῴῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ τὸ ἄλογον μέρος ἐψυχῶσθαί τε καὶ μόριον αὐτῆς εἶναι. αὐτίκα τὴν μὲν ζωτικὴν δύναμιν, ᾗ ἐμπεριέχεται τὸ θρεπτικόν τε καὶ αὐξητικὸν καὶ καθ’ ὅλου κινητικόν, τὸ πνεῦμα εἴληχεν τὸ σαρκικόν, ὀξυκίνητον ὃν καὶ πάντῃ διά τε τῶν αἰσθήσεων καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ σώματος πορευόμενόν τε καὶ πρωτοπαθοῦν διὰ σώματος· τὴν προαιρετικὴν δὲ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἔχει δύναμιν, περὶ ἣν ἡ ζήτησις καὶ ἡ μάθησις καὶ ἡ γνῶσις. ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἡ πάντων ἀναφορὰ εἰς ἓν συντέτακται τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν καὶ δἰ ἐκεῖνο ζῇ τε ὁ ἄνθρωπος καί πως ζῇ.
pass_a_gloss: Let the decalogue be set forth as an example for us, by way of a sidestep, for clear knowledge. And that the ten is sacred, it is superfluous to say now. But if the written tablets are a work of God, they will be found to reveal a natural creation, for the finger of God is considered the power of God, through which the creation of heaven and earth is completed, of which both the tablets will be thought to be symbols. For the writing and shaping of God, left on the tablet, is the creation of the world. The decalogue, on the one hand, contains the heavenly image, sun and moon, stars, clouds, light, spirit, water, air, darkness, and fire. This is the natural decalogue of heaven. The image of the earth, on the other hand, contains humans, animals, reptiles, and beasts, and of the aquatic, fish and sea monsters, and of the birds, similarly, the flesh-eaters and those that use food by day, and of plants, likewise, the fruit-bearing and the barren. This is the natural decalogue of earth. And the ark that contains these things would be the knowledge and wisdom of divine and human things. Perhaps these two tablets would be a twofold prophecy of covenants. They were renewed, therefore, mystically, because of the abundance of ignorance and sin at the same time. It seems that the commands are written twice, with two spirits, the ruling and the subject, since the flesh desires against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. There is also a certain ten concerning the human himself, the five senses and the vocal and the generative, and this, the eighth, is the spiritual according to the formation, and the ninth is the ruling part of the soul, and the tenth is the characteristic of the Holy Spirit, which is added through faith. Furthermore, it seems that the legislation commands ten human parts, sight and hearing and smell and touch and taste, and the two organs that serve them, hands and feet, for this is the formation of the human. The soul is also inscribed and the ruling part is inscribed, by which we reason, not born according to the casting of the seed, so that the tenth number is gathered even without this, through which the whole activity of the human is completed. For the human, being directly in order, takes the beginning of life from the passive. We say, therefore, that the rational and ruling part is the cause of the constitution of the living thing, but also of the irrational part being ensouled and being a part of it. The spirit, therefore, has taken the vital power, by which the nourishing and growing and, in general, moving are enclosed, the bodily spirit, which is quick-moving and goes through all the senses and the rest of the body, and is moved and suffers first through the body. The ruling part, however, has the power of choice, concerning which there is investigation and learning and knowledge. But since the reference of all things is to one, the ruling part is constituted, and through it the human lives and lives in some way.
pass_b_english: We should set out the Decalogue as our example, by way of a brief digression, for the sake of clear knowledge. That the number ten is sacred need not be said now. Yet if the inscribed tablets are a work of God, they will be found to reveal a natural creation, because the finger of God is understood as the power of God through which the creation of heaven and earth is completed, and the tablets themselves will be recognized as symbols of those two realms. For the writing and shaping that God leaves on the tablet amounts to the creation of the world. On the one hand, the Decalogue contains the heavenly image: sun and moon, stars, clouds, light, spirit, water, air, darkness, and fire. This is the natural Decalogue of heaven. On the other hand, the image of the earth contains human beings, cattle, reptiles, wild beasts, and among aquatic creatures fish and sea monsters, and among birds likewise the flesh-eaters and those that feed by day, and among plants likewise the fruit-bearing and the barren. This is the natural Decalogue of earth.

The ark that encloses these things would be the knowledge and wisdom of both divine and human matters. Perhaps these two tablets are a twofold prophecy of covenants. They were therefore renewed mystically, because ignorance and sin abounded together. It appears that the commandments are written twice, by two spirits, the ruling and the subject, since the flesh desires against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. There is also a certain ten that pertains to the human person himself: the five senses, the vocal faculty, and the generative faculty, and this eighth is the spiritual faculty according to the formation; the ninth is the ruling part of the soul; and the tenth is the distinctive mark of the Holy Spirit that is added through faith. Furthermore, the legislation appears to prescribe ten human parts: sight, hearing, smell, touch, and taste, together with the two pairs of organs that serve them, hands and feet, for this is the human formation. The soul is also inscribed, and the ruling part is inscribed, by which we reason, not born according to the casting of the seed, so that the tenth number is assembled even without it, through which the whole activity of the human being is completed. For the human being, coming directly into order, takes the beginning of life from the passive elements. We say, therefore, that the rational and ruling part is the cause of the living thing's constitution, but also of the irrational part being ensouled and becoming a portion of it. The bodily spirit has received the vital power, by which the nourishing, growing, and in general moving functions are enclosed, being quick-moving and passing through all the senses and the rest of the body, and being moved and suffering first through the body. The ruling part, however, possesses the power of choice, concerning which there is investigation, learning, and knowledge. But since the reference of all things is ordered to one, the ruling part is constituted, and through it the human being lives and lives in some way.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological and physiological distinctions made by Clement, including the enumeration of the 'ten' (the senses, organs, and spiritual faculties) and the distinction between the ruling (ἡγεμονικόν) and passive/subject (ὑποκειμένῳ) parts of the human. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
